summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of atrial fibrillation, aortic stenosis, chronic diastolic heart failure, and spinal stenosis was admitted due to altered mental status. He had recently started a fentanyl patch for back pain and had not had a bowel movement in several days. The confusion was attributed to toxic encephalopathy likely caused by the fentanyl, with possible contribution from constipation and mild fluid overload from heart failure. The fentanyl patch was discontinued, a bowel regimen was initiated, and the furosemide dose was increased to 20 mg daily. The patient improved rapidly, regained full orientation, and was discharged to extended care with instructions to avoid fentanyl, continue current pain medications, monitor INR weekly, and discuss starting an ACE inhibitor with his cardiologist.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Other opiates and related narcotics causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
Spondylosis of unspecified site, without mention of myelopathy
